title: Version numbers: three parts set by the release job from the pull request's type
summary: orion's version becomes three parts set by the release job from the merged pull request titles' Conventional Commit types, with a whole-number bridge tag per release for old installs, a pull request title check, and ORION_VERSION removed. Merged on the owner's word because it touches the repository's CLAUDE.md.
friction: An early branch commit used a real pull request title and number from a downstream project as a test string; a later commit removed it, but it stays visible in the pull request's commit list on the host (distribution-safety near miss).
lessons_learned: Version and tag logic in orion.sh needs its edge scenarios tested up front (a decline recorded by update --skip, a tag added after install, a ref other than main, a re-run of an older release job): each of four review rounds found one more of them.

deferred.what: On a computer with one project on the new orion.sh and another on an older one, the older script reads three-part values (the ORION GLOBAL heading, the global-offered-version record, the status line stamp) as no version, so the two projects take turns re-offering the personal rules and the older one can offer its older status line, stepping the computer's copy back.
deferred.why: Older scripts cannot be changed after the fact; a record format they still read is a design choice beyond this story.

deferred.what: The release job sizes each version from squash-commit subjects, but the repository's squash title setting is 'commit or pull request title' and gh pr merge --squash passes no --subject, so a single-commit pull request titled feat(x)!: y whose commit reads feat(x): y ships a breaking change as a minor release.
deferred.why: The fix is a repository setting (the owner's) or a dev-next merge-step change, both outside this story's seam.
